source_text: Ἰγνατιος, ὁ καὶ Θεοφόρος, τῇ ἠλεημένῃ ἐν μεγαλειότητι πατρὸς ὑψίστου καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ μόνου υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἠγαπημένῃ καὶ πεφωτισμένῃ ἐν θελήματι τοῦ θελήσαντος τὰ πάντα, ἃ ἔστιν, κατὰ ἀγάπην Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν, ἥτις καὶ προκάθηται ἐν τόπῳ χωρίου Ῥωμαίων, ἀξιόθεος, ἀξιοπρεπής, ἀξιομακάριστος, ἀξιέπαινος, ἀξιεπίτευκτος, ἀξίαγνος καὶ προκαθημένη τῆς ἀγάπης, χριστώνυμος, πατρώνυμος, ἣν καὶ ἀσπάζομαι ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, υἱοῦ πατρός: κατὰ σάρκα καὶ πνεῦμα ἡνωμένοις πάσῃ ἐντολῇ αὐτοῦ, πεπληρωμένοις χάριτος θεοῦ ἀδιακρίτως καὶ ἀποδιυλισμένοις ἀπὸ παντὸς ἀλλοτρίου χρώματος πλεῖστα ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ, τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν, ἀμώμως χαίρειν.
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to the church in Rome, praising it with a chain of honorific titles and greeting its members in the name of Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Ignatius, the [one] also [called] God-bearer, to the [church] that has received mercy in [the] greatness of [the] Father Most High and of Jesus Christ his only Son, [the church] beloved and enlightened in [the] will of [the one] who willed all things, which exist, according to [the] love of Jesus Christ our God, which also presides in [the] place of [the] region of [the] Romans, worthy of God, worthy of honor, worthy of blessing, worthy of praise, worthy of success, worthy of purity and presiding over [the] love, bearing Christ's name, bearing [the] Father's name, which also I greet in [the] name of Jesus Christ, Son of [the] Father: to [those] united in flesh and spirit to every commandment of his, filled with [the] grace of God without wavering and filtered from every foreign color, most abundantly in Jesus Christ our God, blamelessly, greetings.

choices.why: The epithet means 'bearing God'; rendering it as a compound noun preserves the title's force as a name-like designation.
The perfect passive participle conveys a completed state of having been shown mercy; a finite relative clause makes the sense clear in English.
The compound adjective means 'worthy of God'; a phrase preserves the genitive force of the second element.
The verb means to strain or filter out impurities; 'filtered' keeps the concrete image of purification.
The adverb means 'without division or distinction'; in context it describes unwavering fullness of grace.
The adverb from 'blameless' modifies the greeting, conveying the state in which the recipients are addressed.

pass_b_english: Ignatius, who is also called God-Bearer, to the church that has found mercy in the majesty of the Most High Father and of Jesus Christ, his only Son: to the church beloved and enlightened by the will of the One who willed all things that are, in keeping with the love of Jesus Christ our God; to the church that presides in the land of the Romans, worthy of God, worthy of honor, worthy of blessing, worthy of praise, worthy of success, worthy of purity, presiding over love, bearing the name of Christ and the name of the Father. Her I greet in the name of Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father.

To all who are one in flesh and spirit with every commandment of his, who are filled with the grace of God without wavering and freed from every foreign taint: heartiest greetings, blameless, in Jesus Christ our God.

sweep.held_why: gate: Pass A and Pass B are near-copies; Pass B is still the gloss in source word order. Rewrite the sentences without adding or dropping a claim
previous_english: Ignatius, who is also called God-bearer, greets the church that has received mercy in the majesty of the Father Most High and of Jesus Christ, His only Son. This church is beloved and enlightened by the will of the One who willed all things that exist, according to the love of Jesus Christ our God. She presides in the region of the Romans, worthy of God, worthy of honor, worthy of blessing, worthy of praise, worthy of success, worthy of purity, and she presides over the love, bearing Christ's name and the Father's name. I greet her in the name of Jesus Christ, Son of the Father. To those who are united in flesh and spirit with every commandment of His, filled with the grace of God without wavering and filtered from every foreign color, I wish abundant blameless joy in Jesus Christ our God.
sweep.note: Held twice by the near-copy gate only (no confirmed source problems). Re-shaped from the Greek, every claim kept.

problems.why: Same epithet rendered three ways; reader may think these differ.

problems.quote: strained clean of every foreign color
problems.why: 'Foreign color' is not natural English; reads like a literal gloss of a Greek metaphor about dye or impurity.
problems.fix: Render as 'purified of every alien admixture' or 'freed from every foreign taint.'

edits.old: strained clean of every foreign color

fixed: Standardized 'God-bearer' to 'God-Bearer' to match the epithet's rendering elsewhere.
Changed 'strained clean of every foreign color' to 'freed from every foreign taint' for natural English while preserving the metaphor of purification from impurity.
